fig1_residue_contour.svg: Brightness is $\log_{10}|f|$ for $f=1/(z^2+1)$; the two flares are the poles at $\pm i$. The loop $C$ (winding number $1$ about $+i$, $0$ about $-i$) encloses one pole, so the residue theorem gives $\oint_C f\,dz=2\pi i\,\mathrm{Res}_{+i}f$. Computed with the module: $\mathrm{Res}_{+i}f=-\tfrac{i}{2}$ and $\oint_C f\,dz\approx\pi$.
fig2_cauchy_zn.svg: The unit-circle integral $\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint z^{\,n}\,dz$ from contour_integral, for $n=-3\ldots3$. Every power is $0$ except $n=-1$, which gives $1$: analytic integrands ($n\ge0$) vanish by Cauchy's theorem and higher poles ($n\le-2$) are pure derivatives, so only the $1/z$ term carries a residue — the basis of the residue calculus.
